readMe: Scoping settings for the zvec retrieval lane, read by
This file is NOT a zvec-grep-native config. zvec-grep reads exactly one config
file, the global ~/.zvec-grep/config.json; it has no project-level config and
hard-skips the workspace <root>/.zvec-grep/ directory, which holds generated
index state only. Workspace scoping is therefore an index-time argument set,
stored inside the generated manifest, and the manifest is not reviewable. This
file is the reviewable preimage of that argument set, so the scope a reader
sees is the scope the index was built with.
Changing globs here does not change an existing index. zvec-grep reuses stored
file-selection settings until an explicit --reset-paths or --rebuild.

globNotes.order: Includes first, exclusions last. A later rule overrides an earlier one, so reversing the order re-admits everything the exclusions remove.
globNotes.lineages: Written as **/lineages/** rather than **/research/lineages/**. Fan-out lineage directories are raw per-executor transcripts wherever they sit, and they are the largest low-value tree in the corpus. The narrower spelling would have left most of them indexed.
globNotes.research: research/ itself stays in. research.md and synthesis.md are the distilled artifacts the concept lane exists to find; only the raw lineages under them are dropped.
globNotes.reviewArtifacts: review/, iterations/ and deltas/ are deep-loop run artifacts. They restate their packet's documents per iteration, so indexing them buys duplicate hits that crowd out the source.
globNotes.commandsAndAgents: .opencode/commands/**/*.md and .opencode/agents/**/*.md are deliberately absent. The markdown includes name specs/ and .opencode/skills/ only; command and agent prose is reachable through the ripgrep lane.
